name: Is Cabinet Refacing Better Than Full Replacement for a San Diego Kitchen?

mainEntity.name: When does cabinet refacing make more sense than replacing kitchen cabinets in an older San Diego home?
mainEntity.text: When does cabinet refacing make more sense than replacing kitchen cabinets in an older San Diego home?

acceptedAnswer.text: Cabinet refacing replaces visible doors and drawer fronts while keeping most cabinet boxes. It can work well when the existing layout is functional, boxes are square and dry, and the homeowner wants a new finish without extensive demolition. It may also reduce construction time and preserve flooring or countertops. Full replacement is usually more suitable when cabinets have water damage, weak shelves, warped boxes, poor corner access, inadequate drawer storage, or a layout that creates difficult work zones. Replacement also makes it easier to add pull-outs, deeper drawers, appliance panels, a larger island, or updated clearances. Ask for a condition assessment of every box, face frame, hinge, drawer, and wall attachment. Compare complete pricing, including repairs, veneer matching, hardware, installation, filler panels, trim, painting, countertop removal, and disposal. Check whether refacing changes cabinet dimensions enough to affect appliances or countertops. A low refacing price can become less attractive if damaged boxes, hidden moisture, or custom modifications are excluded.
acceptedAnswer.description: Refacing may suit cabinets with sound boxes, a workable layout, and limited water or structural damage. Replacement is usually better when boxes are warped, swollen, poorly configured, or unable to support modern storage and appliances. Compare the cost of doors, hardware, drawer upgrades, repairs, and finish work with a complete cabinet package.
